info.description:
Configure the Quilr LLM Gateway programmatically: apps, shared providers, quota pools, gateway keys, prompts, budgets and history.

**Authentication.** Tenant administrators enable management for a tenant and issue management keys with the Administration endpoints (verified tenant administrator token). Every other endpoint takes a management key as `Authorization: Bearer qlmgmt_...`. Each operation lists the scopes it requires in `x-scopes`; an empty list on an Administration operation means a verified tenant administrator token.

**Writes.** Updates and deletes of an existing resource require `If-Match` with the quoted `version` (ETag) from the latest read (`428` when missing, `412` when stale). Creates take an `Idempotency-Key`; retrying with the same key replays the original result for 24 hours. Saved configuration reaches the gateway asynchronously.

**Responses.** Every JSON response carries `request_id` (also in `X-Request-ID`) and `Cache-Control: no-store`. Errors use `{"error": {"code", "message", ...}, "request_id"}`. Lists are paginated with `limit` and an opaque `cursor` (`next_cursor` is null on the last page).

**Policy.** General QuilrQL policy authoring is not part of this API. Budget and pricing edits (scope `budgets:policy`) are the only policy-backed writes: each publishes a validated policy revision. When QuilrQL governs a tenant, app settings it governs are saved but take effect only when policy authority is disabled; responses flag them with an `inactive_under_quilrql` warning.

Apps whose names contain `/` or a literal `%` can be addressed with the query-locator aliases under `/app?app_name=...` (marked with `x-alias-of`).

get.description:
Counts what the gateway guardrails did to the tenant's traffic: requests scanned, flagged, blocked, redacted and monitored, and the detections behind them. Group by up to two of `category`, `action`, `direction`, `app`, `user` and `model`, and bucket by `granularity`: total (the default), or UTC `month`, `week` (starting Monday) or `day`. `from` is inclusive and `to` exclusive; a date `to` includes that whole UTC day.

Only counts and identifiers are returned, never prompt or response text or the detected values. Categories are `{id, name, type}`: the ids and display names from app settings and policies; custom definitions use their id and the name you gave them. region.description: `guardrails-usa-1`: USA 1 (US Central West); `guardrails-usa-2`: USA 2 (US East); `guardrails-europe-1`: Europe; `guardrails-india-1`: India 1 (Mumbai); `guardrails-india-2`: India 2 (Mumbai); `guardrails-jp-1`: Japan (Tokyo); `guardrails`: Global

x-scope-descriptions.budgets:grant: Issue, change and revoke budget grants.
x-scope-descriptions.budgets:policy: Edit budgets, pricing, exemptions and alert destinations (publishes a policy revision).
x-scope-descriptions.budgets:read: Read budgets, usage, subjects, grants, pricing, exemptions, alerts and events.
x-scope-descriptions.config:write: Change app settings, attachments, prompts; roll back and recover app writes.
x-scope-descriptions.credentials:read: Reveal the secret of an active gateway key.
x-scope-descriptions.credentials:write: Issue, change expiry of and revoke gateway keys.
x-scope-descriptions.incidents:read: Read incident mark-downs and incident propagation status (read or incidents:write also allow these reads).
x-scope-descriptions.incidents:write: Mark providers down for an incident, preview the impact, restore them, reset cooldowns and drop session pins (tenant-wide, never a policy revision).
x-scope-descriptions.limits:grant: Issue and revoke temporary rate limit raises.
x-scope-descriptions.limits:read: Read rate limits, request guards, model limits, exemptions, limit responses, live usage, grants and effective limits.
x-scope-descriptions.limits:write: Change rate limits, request guards, model limits, exemptions and limit responses, and migrate legacy limits (each write publishes a policy revision).
x-scope-descriptions.providers:write: Create, update and delete shared providers and quota pools; run provider tests and model discovery.
x-scope-descriptions.read: Read apps, providers, quota pools, credentials metadata, prompts, catalogs, history and this document.
x-scope-descriptions.routing:constraints: Change routing constraints (hard placement and capability limits).
x-scope-descriptions.routing:read: Read routing controls (routes, destinations, failover, routing constraints, model access), policy capacity and revision rollout, and run the routing diagnostics (effective route, test routing, target check, routing and failover summaries).
x-scope-descriptions.routing:write: Change routes, destinations, failover profiles, rules and default, and model access (each write publishes a policy revision).
